# Flowstate lessons

Full entries (what went wrong, why) are in `~/.claude/lessons-learned.md` under the same date.

- 2026-10-04: A probe that spawns servers exits through `finally` on SIGTERM and runs `pgrep` for its children
  after every `pkill`; rotate clips so the llama-server prompt cache never answers a timing probe (check prompt_n).
- 2026-10-04: msync(MS_INVALIDATE) cannot drop pages that a running server maps; check any eviction step with
  `mincore` first. Reading 10 GB of other model files (cat) reproduces the idle-server slowdown without swap.
- 2026-10-04: Guard a memory-pressure run on used swap and free disk before each trial; this Mac has 2-3 GB free.
- 2026-10-04: Measure a key-down warm-up on a warm server for each engine at the 0.25 s minimum hold:
  whisper-server cost 0.41 s (30 s window, one request at a time), the llama-server and Parakeet engines 0.03-0.08 s.
- 2026-10-04: fcntl F_RDADVISE leaves 69-87% of a 1.6 GB model resident under pressure and loses more within
  seconds; mincore plus pread keeps 100% in the same 0.4 s. Measure a kernel hint's own effect under the target condition.
- 2026-10-04: Keep the STT vocabulary prompt computed at release: the auto-learn read-back at key-down can add a term.
- 2026-10-04: A verification subagent's prompt forbids deleting files (an `rm -rf` prompt blocked one for 40 min);
  at its deadline, read its transcript's last write time.
- 2026-10-04: In zsh, loop over pids from an array or the command output (an unquoted scalar does not split); after a kill, check the pids are gone before the app starts and adopts listeners.
- 2026-10-04: A test assertion must make the path it names run: the prewarm squatter check passed while the
  prewarm probed a fresh port with no squatter. Prove each new check with a mutation that turns it red.
- 2026-10-04: A latency bound in a doc counts every wait on the path (probe timeouts too, 1 s each), and every
  number in a doc comment goes into tasks/todo.md with its run.
- 2026-10-04: Return the value a check verified (the port) from the locked decision; a caller that reads shared
  state after the check can act on a later start's state.

### Steps

- Rewrote the recording pill (`Sources/MurmurKit/RecordingHUD.swift`) as a dark 44 pt capsule: live 7 bar waveform while listening, spinner while transcribing, SF Symbol glyphs for inserted, error, and secure input copy; fade in and out; width follows the text.
- Added mic level metering (`AudioRecorder.meterLevel`, `onLevel` callback) and a pure `WaveformBars` model, wired through `AppController` to the HUD.
- Wrote 21 tests first (red on build), then implemented; checked each state with screenshots and corrected label truncation and square corner halo.
- Rebuilt, installed, and relaunched `~/Applications/Flowstate.app`.

### Done

- 1147 tests pass, 0 fail; verified with `swift run MurmurTests`.
- 0 compiler warnings from Sources; verified with `swift build`.
- All 6 HUD states render with full text and clean capsule corners; verified by screenshot of a demo binary built against MurmurKit.
- App installed and running with the new HUD; verified with `scripts/make_app.sh` and `pgrep -x Flowstate` (printed "relaunched").
- The waveform follows the live mic level in the real app; assumed (the tap path is covered by the meterLevel tests, the running app was not exercised by a dictation).

### Not done

- Nothing committed; your earlier uncommitted edits in ChildServer, the engines, README, and tests are untouched and sit beside this change.
